entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How do proportional rates produce exponential growth and decay?

entries.mainLearnerQuestion: How does a family of primitives become one curve?

syllabusActions.text: Define a primitive of a function f ( x ) as a function F ( x ) whose derivative F ' x = f ( x ) and recognise the process of finding the primitive as the reverse of differentiation
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Define a primitive of a function f(x) as a function F(x) whose derivative F'x=f(x) and recognise the process of finding the primitive as the reverse of differentiation

syllabusActions.text: Recognise that a function whose derivative is everywhere zero is a constant function
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Recognise that a function whose derivative is everywhere zero is a constant function

syllabusActions.text: Prove by differentiation that a primitive of f x = x n is F x = x n + 1 n + 1 , for all real n ≠ - 1
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Prove by differentiation that a primitive of fx=xn is Fx=xn+1n+1, for all real n≠-1

syllabusActions.text: Prove by differentiation that if F ( x ) and G ( x ) are primitives of f ( x ) and g ( x ) , and k is a constant , then F x + G ( x ) is a primitive of f x + g ( x ) , and kF ( x ) is a primitive of kf ( x )
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Prove by differentiation that if F(x) and G(x) are primitives of f(x) and g(x), and k is a constant, then Fx+G(x) is a primitive of fx+g(x), and kF(x) is a primitive of kf(x)

syllabusActions.text: Recognise that primitives of a function f ( x ) are not unique, and that any two primitives of f ( x ) differ by a constant, so that if F ( x ) is a primitive of f ( x ) , the general primitive of f ( x ) is F x + C , for some constant C
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Recognise that primitives of a function f(x) are not unique, and that any two primitives of f(x) differ by a constant, so that if F(x) is a primitive of f(x), the general primitive of f(x) is Fx+C, for some constant C

syllabusActions.text: Determine the primitive of a given function f ( x ) , where f ( x ) is a sum of functions of the form k x n for all real n ≠ - 1

syllabusActions.text: Determine f ( x ) , given f ' ( x ) and an initial condition f ( a ) = b where a and b are constants

syllabusActions.text: Use the notation ∫ f x d x for the general primitive of f x , called the indefinite integral of f x , so that ∫ f x d x = F x + C , for some constant C , where F ( x ) is any primitive of f ( x )
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Use the notation ∫fxdx for the general primitive of fx, called the indefinite integral of fx, so that ∫fxdx=Fx+C, for some constant C, where F(x) is any primitive of f(x)

syllabusActions.text: Recognise integration as the process of finding the indefinite integral of a function
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Recognise integration as the process of finding the indefinite integral of a function

syllabusActions.text: Use the identities ∫ f x + g x d x = ∫ f ( x ) d x + ∫ g ( x ) d x and ∫ k f ( x ) d x = k ∫ f ( x ) d x for primitives
syllabusActions.sourceHtml: Use the identities ∫fx+gxdx=∫f(x)dx+∫g(x)dx and ∫kf(x)dx=k∫f(x)dx for primitives

entryKnowledge.text: Use the formula d dx ( x n ) = n x n - 1 for all real values of n
